findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — [P1, confidence 100] `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;` treats the credential-sync endpoint's Fetch `Response` as Google's `{ data }` SDK response, so every expired synced Google credential hits `TypeError` before installing the refreshed token and calendar operations continue with the expired credential.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — [P1, confidence 100] `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema); ... data: { key },` persists Zod's `SafeParseSuccess` envelope (`{ success, data }`) instead of the parsed credential object, so the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` rejects every Google credential after its first successful local refresh.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — [P1, confidence 100] `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` casts the credential-sync endpoint's Fetch `Response` to a HubSpot token object, so `expiresIn` and `accessToken` are undefined, the database is overwritten with a non-token response object, and the HubSpot client receives an undefined access token whenever sync is enabled.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5 — [P1, confidence 100] `const minimumTokenResponseSchema = z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })` creates literal `[object Object]` keys rather than a dynamic numeric-field schema and strips every real expiry/refresh field, after which `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` replaces a usable refresh token with a sentinel and makes the following refresh fail authentication.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — [P1, confidence 100] `await prisma.credential.update({ ... key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token } });` persists the refreshed Salesforce access token but lines 101-107 construct the live connection from `credentialKey.access_token`, so the operation that triggered refresh still authenticates with the expired token and fails.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — [P2, confidence 75] `const appCredential = await prisma.credential.findFirst(...)` followed by a separate `credential.create` is an unguarded check-then-insert, so concurrent deliveries for the same user and app both observe no row and create duplicate credentials that downstream `findFirst` callers resolve nondeterministically.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — [P2 advisory, confidence 100] `const refreshOAuthTokens = async (refreshFunction: () => any, ... )` returns unrelated provider SDK objects and Fetch `Response` objects behind `any`, so each new integration must duplicate branch-specific shape knowledge and the already-observed Google and HubSpot contract mismatches recur; although provider diversity argues for a generic helper, returning one normalized typed token payload deletes the per-caller response-shape branches and unsafe casts.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:72 — [P3 advisory, confidence 75] `if (appCredential) { ... data: { key: keys } } else { ... appId: appMetadata.slug, type: appMetadata.type }` maintains `type` only on inserts, so an existing credential retains stale routing metadata when an app's canonical type changes; although types are stable today, updating all metadata in one upsert-style write removes the divergent insert/update field lists and the next metadata rename cannot strand existing users.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — [confidence 100, P1] `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT)` omits the sibling `userId` gate used by `refreshOAuthTokens`, so team credentials that deliberately bypass shared refresh are still parsed with the shared endpoint's weak schema and receive the fabricated `"refresh_token"` value instead of enforcing their provider schema.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — [confidence 100, P1] `const response = await fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", {` bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so Salesforce credentials never use `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` while every other refreshed integration added by this change does, leaving the credential-sync feature incomplete for a touched OAuth provider.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:9 — [confidence 100, P1] `const appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema = z.object({` introduces a security-sensitive create/update endpoint with no repository test covering its disabled flag, secret rejection, malformed ciphertext, missing user/app, update, or create branches, so regressions in the feature's acceptance paths ship without verification; the strongest counterargument that generic API infrastructure tests cover routing fails because no existing test references this route or its new helpers.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — [P1, confidence 100] `const token = res?.data;` reads an Axios-style `data` property from the Fetch `Response` returned by the credential-sync branch, so enabling `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` makes every Google token refresh throw while dereferencing `token.access_token` instead of consuming the endpoint JSON.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — [P1, confidence 100] When credential sharing is enabled, `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;` treats the Fetch `Response` returned by `refreshOAuthTokens` as a Google API response, throws on `token.access_token`, and the catch at line 108 silently returns the client with its expired token so calendar operations proceed with stale authentication.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29 — [P1, confidence 100] `return refreshTokenResponse;` returns the Zod safe-parse wrapper instead of parsed token data, so Google stores `{ success, data }` as the credential key at CalendarService.ts:100 and every subsequent credential parse fails instead of using the refreshed token.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — [P1, confidence 100] `await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, {` has no timeout or abort signal, so a stalled credential-sync service holds every token-dependent calendar request open indefinitely and exhausts request workers.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:34 — [P2, confidence 100] `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws an uncaught ZodError for malformed webhook payloads, returning a raw 500 instead of the 4xx client-error response required for invalid input.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:59 — [P2, confidence 100] `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""))` lets invalid ciphertext, a missing key, or non-JSON plaintext escape as an uncaught exception, returning a raw 500 instead of an actionable 4xx webhook rejection.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — [P1, confidence 100] `if (req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET)` authenticates a request with no header when `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset because both operands are `undefined`, letting an unauthenticated caller create or overwrite arbitrary users' OAuth credentials whenever credential sharing is enabled.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30 — [P1, confidence 100] `if (state?.teamId) {` routes any accepted member into team credential creation without calling the imported admin-access check, so a non-admin team member can install attacker-controlled shared credentials for the entire team.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — [P1, confidence 75] `const response = await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId: userId.toString(), appSlug, }), });` requests OAuth access tokens using only predictable user and app identifiers and no authentication credential, so any caller that reaches the configured sync endpoint can request another user's integration token.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that refreshOAuthTokens returns `any` type and different callers receive different response types (Google returns SDK response objects, HubSpot returns token objects, fetch-based integrations return Response objects). Looking at the diff, Google's CalendarService.ts line 86-93 expects `res?.data.access_token`, while office365calendar expects to call `handleErrorsJson(response)` on the return value. This type inconsistency is real and creates maintenance burden, but it's not a bug since the code works - each caller knows what type to expect. adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:72 — [P3 advisory, confidence 75] `if (appCredential) { ... data: { key: keys } } else { ... appId: appMetadata.slug, type: appMetadata.type }` maintains `type` only on inserts, so an existing credential retains stale routing metadata when an app's canonical type changes; although types are stable today, updating all metadata in one upsert-style write removes the divergent insert/update field lists and the next metadata rename cannot strand existing users.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's a problem with 'type' only being set on inserts and not updates, suggesting stale metadata when app types change. However, looking at the diff, the code correctly handles two different scenarios: (1) updating existing credentials only needs to update the 'key' field since the credential already has the correct appId and type, and (2) creating new credentials needs all fields including type. The 'type' field is part of the credential's identity/routing and shouldn't change for an existing credential - it's tied to the app installation. The finding is speculating about a hypothetical future scenario where app types might change, which is not a real bug in the current code. The update only modifying 'key' is intentional and correct behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — [confidence 100, P1] `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT)` omits the sibling `userId` gate used by `refreshOAuthTokens`, so team credentials that deliberately bypass shared refresh are still parsed with the shared endpoint's weak schema and receive the fabricated `"refresh_token"` value instead of enforcing their provider schema.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies an inconsistency between parseRefreshTokenResponse and refreshOAuthTokens. Looking at the diff: refreshOAuthTokens (line 4-5) checks `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` before using the shared endpoint.
